app_purpose: XML parser library used by a real Ruby web app that parses user-supplied XML over HTTP

v0.ref: official image ruby:2.1.3 (loaded into daemon as ruby:2.1.3-official via skopeo). Bundled REXML pre CVE-2014-8080: Entity#value uncapped, no Document#document. Confirmed in-image: entity.rb has NO 'grown too large', document.rb has NO 'def document'.

v1.ref: official image ruby:2.1.4 (ruby:2.1.4-official). CVE-2014-8080 fix: per-value byte cap in lib/rexml/entity.rb Entity#value (raise 'entity expansion has grown too large' at entity.rb:145). document.rb still has NO 'def document' -> count limit still skipped during DTD parse = INCOMPLETE.

v2.ref: official image ruby:2.1.5 (ruby:2.1.5-official). CVE-2014-8090 fix: adds Document#document => self in lib/rexml/document.rb (line 281), so record_entity_expansion runs during DTD parse and the 10000 COUNT limit fires ('number of entity expansions exceeded, processing aborted.' at document.rb:277).

build.strategy: REAL bundled REXML behind a REAL Ruby web app. Base = OFFICIAL ruby:2.1.3/2.1.4/2.1.5 image per profile (build-arg RUBY_VER), so REXML is the exact library shipped in that MRI patch release (verified 3.1.7.3 with the entity.rb/document.rb source differing by patch level). WEBrick (stdlib 1.3.1) app parses user XML over HTTP. NO lifted/vendored REXML source; NO in-process trigger.
build.image_load_note: The 2016-era official ruby:2.1.x images ship a schema-v1 (application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws) manifest that modern Docker (v29) refuses to pull. They are converted schema-v1 -> v2 and loaded straight into the local daemon with: skopeo copy --override-os linux --override-arch amd64 docker://docker.io/library/ruby:<ver> docker-daemon:ruby:<ver>-official . Build uses the legacy builder (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0) so the daemon-loaded bases resolve.
build.host_safety: each profile CPU-pinned (cpus=1.0) + mem_limit 1200m; the DoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measured as server-side latency under a 10s client read timeout. The residual is a pure-CPU count-bomb (empty entities, flat memory), so it hangs (never OOMs the host); the original is memory-bounded by mem_limit. Fresh server per probe (kill + up -d) so a wedged CPU spin can't poison the next measurement.

flag.resource: web-app availability (CPU/latency of POST /parse -> REXML::Document.new on attacker XML)

flag.detect: DoS iff the /parse request hangs (HTTP read timeout) OR crashes the server (mem exhaustion -> connection reset after /health was up) OR server-side latency > T_SLOW(2000ms); BOUNDED iff it returns < T_FAST(500ms) with status in {parsed, limited}

web_app.route: POST /parse  (body = raw XML)  ->  require 'rexml/document'; REXML::Document.new(request.body); each_recursive text expansion
web_app.note: REXML kept at stock 2014 defaults (entity_expansion_limit=10000, entity_expansion_text_limit=10240); not relaxed.

mechanism.summary: REXML has two entity-expansion guards: a text-SIZE cap (entity_expansion_text_limit=10240 bytes) and an expansion-COUNT cap (entity_expansion_limit=10000, via Document#record_entity_expansion, invoked from Entity#unnormalized only `unless document.nil?`). CVE-2014-8080 (V1=2.1.4) added the text-size cap to the PARAMETER-entity value-expansion sink (Entity#value) which V0=2.1.3 left uncapped. That cap is per-value (a fresh local `sum` each call): it bounds SIZE at one level but not the NUMBER of expansions. CVE-2014-8090 residual: expansion triggered inside the internal DTD subset runs while the Document has NO root element, so Document#document (inherited Element#document = root.parent) returns nil, so record_entity_expansion / the COUNT limit is NEVER invoked. Using EMPTY nested parameter entities keeps every expansion under the byte-cap (sum stays 0) while making the COUNT 2**depth -> unbounded CPU on V1. CVE-2014-8090 (V2=2.1.5) adds Document#document => self, so record_entity_expansion runs and the 10000-count limit fires.
mechanism.residual_sink: Document#record_entity_expansion COUNT limit, unreachable during DTD parse because Document#document==nil (lib/rexml/document.rb)
mechanism.guard_v1_observed: V1 original -> RuntimeError 'entity expansion has grown too large' at /usr/local/lib/ruby/2.1.0/rexml/entity.rb:145 (CVE-2014-8080 text cap)
mechanism.guard_v2_observed: V2 residual -> RuntimeError 'number of entity expansions exceeded, processing aborted.' at /usr/local/lib/ruby/2.1.0/rexml/document.rb:277 record_entity_expansion (CVE-2014-8090 count limit)
mechanism.original_attack_xml: payloads/original_attack.xml — nested PARAMETER entities a..j (10x/level) + <root>&bomb;</root> (byte bomb)
mechanism.residual_attack_xml: payloads/residual_attack.xml — EMPTY nested parameter entities a0..a30 + %trigger referenced inside the internal DTD subset (count bomb, flat memory)

provenance.notes: Rebuilt 2026-07-15 to the HARD POLICY: real published REXML as bundled in real Ruby (official ruby:2.1.3/2.1.4/2.1.5 images, REXML 3.1.7.3) inside a REAL WEBrick web app; DoS triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP POST /parse and measured as server-side latency. No in-process trigger, no lifted REXML source. Confirmed on real Docker (legacy builder over skopeo-loaded schema-v1 bases): V0 hangs on both attacks; V1 bounds the CVE-2014-8080 parameter-entity byte bomb (entity.rb:145 'grown too large', 14ms) but the CVE-2014-8090 count-limit-bypass residual still hangs (10s timeout); V2 bounds the residual via document.rb:277 record_entity_expansion ('number of entity expansions exceeded', 58ms). Same mechanism family (entity-expansion DoS); incompleteness = the CVE-2014-8080 text cap is per-value and the COUNT limit was unreachable during DTD parse (document==nil), which CVE-2014-8090 fixes with Document#document=>self.
